textEn: Which was the first commission to touch upon the issues of higher education in India indirectly?
textHi: भारत में उच्च शिक्षा के मुद्दों पर अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से विचार करने वाला पहला आयोग कौन सा था?
explanationEn:
The Indian Education Commission (1882-83):

Also known as the Hunter Commission, it was set up to review the progress of education in India after the introduction of the Woods Despatch (1854).

While its primary focus was on primary and secondary education, it indirectly touched upon the issues of higher education, making it the first commission to do so.

It emphasized improving access to education at all levels and laid the foundation for subsequent reforms in higher education.

The Indian Universities Commission (1902):

This commission was specifically set up to look into the affairs of Indian universities and propose reforms for higher education.

The Calcutta University Commission (1917-1919):

Also known as the Sadler Commission, it was formed to specifically address the challenges faced by universities and improve higher education.

The Hartog Committee (1929):

Focused on examining the overall progress in education, particularly primary and secondary education, but also touched upon higher education efficiency.

textHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा समझौता/प्रोटोकॉल मुख्य रूप से वैश्विक तापमान वृद्धि को रोकने पर केंद्रित है?
explanationEn:
Paris Agreement:

Adopted in 2015 at the 21st Conference of the Parties (COP21) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

Its primary goal is to limit global warming to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels, with efforts to limit the increase to 1.5°C.

The agreement emphasizes reducing greenhouse gas emissions, enhancing global efforts for climate resilience, and providing financial support to developing nations to address climate change.

It represents a unified global effort to combat climate change by setting nationally determined contributions (NDCs).

Montreal Protocol:

Focuses on phasing out substances that deplete the ozone layer, such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).

Although it indirectly benefits climate by reducing potent greenhouse gases, its primary aim is not related to global temperature rise.

Kigali Agreement:

A 2016 amendment to the Montreal Protocol, it aims to phase down hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), potent greenhouse gases.

While it addresses climate change indirectly by targeting HFCs, its focus is narrower than the Paris Agreement.

Kyoto Protocol:

Adopted in 1997 under the UNFCCC, it set legally binding targets for industrialized countries to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

While it focuses on emissions reduction, it lacks the broader, inclusive goals of limiting global temperature rise as outlined in the Paris Agreement.

यह समझौता ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जन को कम करने, जलवायु लचीलेपन के लिए वैश्विक प्रयासों को बढ़ाने और जलवायु परिवर्तन से निपटने के लिए विकासशील देशों को वित्तीय सहायता प्रदान करने पर जोर देता है।

यद्यपि यह अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से शक्तिशाली ग्रीनहाउस गैसों को कम करके जलवायु को लाभ पहुंचाता है, लेकिन इसका प्राथमिक उद्देश्य वैश्विक तापमान वृद्धि से संबंधित नहीं है।

(B) Reviewing of hopes and aspirations

(C) Increased ability to understand

(D) Increased ability to generalize the facts

(E) Ability of problem solving

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
textHi:
निम्नलिखित में से किशोरों के मानसिक विकास की कौन सी विशेषताएँ हैं?

(ए) अमूर्तता से निपटने की क्षमता में वृद्धि

(बी) आशाओं और आकांक्षाओं की समीक्षा

(सी) समझने की क्षमता में वृद्धि

(डी) तथ्यों को सामान्यीकृत करने की क्षमता में वृद्धि

(ई) समस्या समाधान की क्षमता

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:
explanationEn:
• Here’s the explanation of each characteristic of mental development in adolescents:

(A) Increased ability to deal with abstraction: Adolescents develop the ability to think more abstractly. They move beyond concrete thinking and are able to handle complex ideas and concepts, such as hypothetical situations or philosophical concepts. This is a key cognitive development during adolescence.

(C) Increased ability to understand: Adolescents exhibit enhanced cognitive abilities, such as better comprehension of complex information. Their ability to understand abstract concepts, relationships, and different perspectives also improves as they mature.

(D) Increased ability to generalize the facts: Adolescents begin to generalize facts from one situation to another. They develop the ability to apply learned principles and facts in new contexts, reflecting their growing cognitive flexibility and understanding.

(E) Ability of problem solving: Adolescents experience an increase in problem- solving skills. They become more capable of addressing complex problems, considering multiple solutions, and analyzing various outcomes. Their cognitive skills allow them to approach challenges in a more sophisticated manner.

• The characteristic (B) Reviewing of hopes and aspirations is more related to emotional and social development rather than strictly mental development. While it is an important aspect of adolescence, it does not fit as directly into cognitive development as the other options.

• Thus, the correct answer is (3) (A), (C), (D) and (E) only.

textHi: पेचिश एक जलजनित रोग है जो दूषित जल से होता है:
explanationEn:
Dysentery is a waterborne disease typically caused by bacterial

infections, although it can also be caused by protozoa in some cases.

The bacterial form of dysentery is most commonly caused by

Shigella bacteria, which infects the intestines, leading to symptoms

such as diarrhea, abdominal pain, and fever. The infection spreads

through contaminated water, food, or direct contact with fecal

matter from infected individuals.

In addition to bacterial dysentery, there is a form caused by

Entamoeba histolytica, a protozoan parasite, which leads to

amoebic dysentery. This type of dysentery is also transmitted

through contaminated water or food. However, the most common

cause, particularly in areas with poor sanitation, is the bacterial type.

Contaminated water sources, often due to inadequate sanitation and

hygiene practices, are the primary vectors for both types of

dysentery. Consuming water or food that has been exposed to fecal

contamination is the main way these pathogens enter the human

body.

Thus, while both bacteria and protozoa can cause dysentery, the

most widespread form is typically caused by bacteria. Therefore, the

correct answer is (2) Bacteria.

textEn: A sampling technique that relies on getting information from people who know about a population of interest rather than from members of that population themselves, refers to?
textHi: एक नमूना तकनीक जो उस आबादी के सदस्यों के बजाय रुचि की आबादी के बारे में जानने वाले लोगों से जानकारी प्राप्त करने पर निर्भर करती है, उसे संदर्भित करती है?
explanationEn:
Key informant sampling is a non-probability sampling technique where

information is gathered from individuals who have specialized knowledge or

expertise about a particular population of interest, rather than directly from

the members of the population themselves. These individuals, known as key

informants, are typically selected based on their knowledge, experience, or

position within a specific community or subject area.

This technique is particularly useful when studying hard-to-reach populations

or when direct access to the population is difficult. Key informants can provide

valuable insights, background information, or detailed descriptions that help

researchers understand the characteristics, behaviors, or social dynamics of

the population. It is commonly used in qualitative research, ethnographic

studies, and when exploring niche groups where direct surveys or interviews

might be impractical or impossible.

While snowball sampling (option 3) involves the recruitment of participants

through referrals from initial participants, key informant sampling specifically

relies on the expert knowledge of selected individuals, which makes it distinct

in its purpose and application.

Thus, key informant sampling is a valuable method for gathering expert

insights, especially in research contexts where understanding the broader

population through a select group of knowledgeable individuals is essential.

explanationEn:
A forced log-off feature is a security measure designed to minimize

the risk of unauthorized access or breaches by automatically logging

out a user if no activity is detected within a set period. This is

particularly useful in preventing attackers from taking advantage of

unattended sessions. For instance, if a user forgets to log out or

walks away from their computer, the system will automatically

terminate the session, reducing the chances of someone else

accessing sensitive data or compromising the system.

This feature helps enhance the security of the computer system by

limiting the window of opportunity for unauthorized users to gain

access to an active session. It is commonly used in environments

where sensitive information is accessed, such as in healthcare,

banking, and governmental organizations.

Other options, such as allowing the installation of software of the

user's choice or enabling file uploads and downloads, may introduce

security vulnerabilities if not properly controlled. Similarly, logging

into multiple nodes using one account can increase the risk of

misuse or unauthorized access, making option (3) the most effective

measure for preventing security breaches.

textEn: The N.N. Kunzru committee was formed to look into the issue of …………. at the university level.
textHi: एन.एन. ………… के मुद्दे को देखने के लिए कुंजरू समिति का गठन किया गया था। विश्वविद्यालय स्तर पर.
explanationEn:
The N.N. Kunzru Committee was formed in 1964 to examine and make recommendations regarding the medium of instruction in Indian universities. During that time, there was a growing debate about whether English or regional languages should be used as the medium of instruction at the university level. The committee was tasked with studying the situation and providing suggestions for a balanced approach that could support educational development across India, considering both the national language and the regional linguistic diversity.

The committee recognized the importance of preserving regional languages while also acknowledging the role of English as a global language of academia and business. The recommendations aimed to create a framework for the use of both English and regional languages in education, thus ensuring that students could gain access to modern knowledge while also promoting the use of their mother tongues.

The issue of medium of instruction was particularly crucial in post- independence India, where the linguistic diversity was vast, and the need for educational reform was significant. Therefore, the N.N. Kunzru Committee's focus was on addressing how the language of instruction could best serve the educational needs of a diverse population.

textEn:
Identify the main preoccupations of quantitative researchers:

(A) Measurement

(B) Causality

(C) Emphasis on context

(D) Generalization

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
textHi:
मात्रात्मक शोधकर्ताओं की मुख्य व्यस्तताओं की पहचान करें:

(ए) माप

(बी) कारणता

(सी) संदर्भ पर जोर

(डी) सामान्यीकरण

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:
explanationEn:
Quantitative researchers typically focus on the following key aspects:

(A) Measurement: Measurement is a fundamental aspect of quantitative research.

Researchers aim to quantify variables in a systematic, reliable, and valid way. This

involves using tools like surveys, scales, tests, and instruments to assign numerical

values to variables, making the research objective and reproducible.

(B) Causality: Quantitative research often seeks to establish causal relationships

between variables. Researchers aim to determine whether one variable causes

changes in another, typically using methods like experiments, longitudinal studies,

or statistical analysis. Causality is central to many quantitative studies as it helps

explain the dynamics between different variables.

(D) Generalization: A primary goal of quantitative research is to generalize findings

from a sample to a larger population. By using random sampling and large sample

sizes, researchers can make inferences about the broader population with a certain

level of confidence. This emphasis on generalization ensures that the results have

relevance beyond the specific context of the study.

While (C) Emphasis on context is important in some types of research, it is not

typically a major focus of quantitative research. Instead, quantitative researchers

tend to emphasize objectivity, measurement, and generalizability, which may not

always prioritize the specific context of the study. This makes option (3) the most

appropriate choice.

textEn: Which of the following statements is true?
textHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सत्य है?
optionsEn: In a valid argument all of its premises have to be true
Validity can be attributed to any single proposition by itself
Truth and falsehood are attributes of single propositions
Truth and falsehood can be attributed to arguments
optionsHi: एक वैध तर्क में इसके सभी आधार सत्य होने चाहिए
वैधता का श्रेय किसी एक प्रस्ताव को ही दिया जा सकता है
सत्य और असत्य एकल प्रस्ताव के गुण हैं
सत्य और असत्य का श्रेय तर्कों को दिया जा सकता है
explanationEn:
In logic, truth and falsehood are properties that apply to individual

propositions or statements, not to entire arguments. A proposition is a

declarative sentence that can be either true or false. For example, the

statement "The sky is blue" is a proposition, and it can either be true or false

depending on the actual state of the sky.

However, validity is a property of an argument, not individual propositions. An

argument is valid if, assuming all the premises are true, the conclusion must

also be true. Importantly, a valid argument doesn't require the premises to be

true in the real world; it only requires that the logical structure is such that the

truth of the premises guarantees the truth of the conclusion.

Therefore:

Statement (1) is incorrect because validity does not require all premises to be

true, only logically sound (i.e., the conclusion follows from the premises).

Statement (2) is incorrect because validity applies to the entire argument, not

to individual propositions.

Statement (4) is incorrect because arguments cannot be true or false; they are

valid or invalid based on their logical structure.

Thus, Statement (3) is the correct one because it correctly identifies that truth

and falsehood apply to individual propositions, not to arguments.

कथन "आकाश नीला है" एक प्रस्ताव है, और यह या तो सत्य या गलत हो सकता है

हालाँकि, वैधता एक तर्क की संपत्ति है, व्यक्तिगत प्रस्तावों की नहीं। एक

तर्क वैध है यदि, यह मानते हुए कि सभी आधार सत्य हैं, निष्कर्ष अवश्य होना चाहिए

सच भी हो. महत्वपूर्ण बात यह है कि एक वैध तर्क के लिए परिसर की आवश्यकता नहीं होती है

वास्तविक दुनिया में सच; इसके लिए केवल यह आवश्यक है कि तार्किक संरचना ऐसी हो कि

परिसर की सत्यता निष्कर्ष की सत्यता की गारंटी देती है।

कथन (1) गलत है क्योंकि वैधता के लिए सभी परिसरों की आवश्यकता नहीं होती है

सत्य, केवल तार्किक रूप से सही (अर्थात, निष्कर्ष परिसर से निकलता है)।

कथन (2) गलत है क्योंकि वैधता पूरे तर्क पर लागू होती है, नहीं

व्यक्तिगत प्रस्तावों के लिए.

कथन (4) ग़लत है क्योंकि तर्क सत्य या ग़लत नहीं हो सकते; वे हैं

उनकी तार्किक संरचना के आधार पर वैध या अमान्य।

इस प्रकार, कथन (3) सही है क्योंकि यह उस सत्य की सही पहचान करता है

और झूठ व्यक्तिगत प्रस्तावों पर लागू होता है, तर्कों पर नहीं।

textEn: Travelling in a train, a man notices 13 telephone poles in two minutes. If the two successive telephone poles are known to be 125 m a part, then the train is travelling at a speed of:
textHi: ट्रेन में यात्रा करते समय, एक आदमी दो मिनट में 13 टेलीफोन खंभों को देखता है। यदि दो क्रमिक टेलीफोन खंभों को 125 मीटर का भाग माना जाता है, तो ट्रेन की गति से यात्रा कर रही है:
explanationEn:
Step 1: Total distance covered

The man observes 13 telephone poles, meaning there are 12 gaps between the poles.

Each gap is 125 meters.

So, total distance = 12 × 125 = 1500 meters.

Step 2: Time taken

The time given is 2 minutes. Convert this to seconds:

Time = 2 × 60 = 120 seconds.

Step 3: Speed in meters per second

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed = 1500 ÷ 120 = 12.5 m/s

Step 4: Convert speed to kilometers per hour

To convert from meters per second to kilometers per hour, multiply by 3.6:

Speed = 12.5 × 3.6 = 45 km/hr.
explanationHi:
चरण 1: तय की गई कुल दूरी

आदमी 13 टेलीफोन खंभों को देखता है, जिसका अर्थ है कि खंभों के बीच 12 अंतराल हैं।

प्रत्येक गैप 125 मीटर है।

अतः, कुल दूरी = 12 × 125 = 1500 मीटर।

चरण 2: लिया गया समय

2 मिनट का समय दिया गया है. इसे सेकंड में बदलें:

समय = 2 × 60 = 120 सेकंड.

चरण 3: गति मीटर प्रति सेकंड में

गति = दूरी ÷ समय

गति = 1500 ÷ 120 = 12.5 मी/से

चरण 4: गति को किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे में बदलें

मीटर प्रति सेकंड से किलोमीटर प्रति घंटा में बदलने के लिए 3.6 से गुणा करें:

गति = 12.5 × 3.6 = 45 किमी/घंटा

explanationEn:
Measures of dispersion are statistical tools used to describe the spread or variability

of a data set. They give an idea of how much individual data points differ from the

central value (mean or median). The following are the measures of dispersion:

Mean Deviation (A): This measures the average of the absolute differences between

each data point and the mean of the data set. It is a common measure of dispersion.

Standard Deviation (C): This is a widely used measure that quantifies the amount of

variation or spread in a data set. It is based on the squared differences from the

mean and provides insight into how spread out the data is.

Range (D): This is the difference between the highest and lowest values in a data

set. It is the simplest measure of dispersion.

The Median (B) and Quartile (E) are not measures of dispersion:

Median: It is a measure of central tendency, not dispersion. It represents the middle

value of a data set when arranged in ascending order.

Quartiles: These divide the data set into four equal parts, but are not considered a

direct measure of dispersion by themselves. However, the interquartile range (IQR),

which is the difference between the first and third quartiles, is a measure of

dispersion.

Therefore, the correct answer is (A), (C), and (D).

textEn: "Of course, abortion has to be legal. After all, a woman must have freedom to do whatever she wants with her own body". Identify the fallacy committed in this statement:
textHi: "बेशक, गर्भपात को कानूनी होना ही चाहिए। आख़िरकार, एक महिला को अपने शरीर के साथ जो चाहे करने की आज़ादी होनी चाहिए"। इस कथन में की गई भ्रांति को पहचानें:
explanationEn:
The statement "Of course, abortion has to be legal. After all, a woman must have freedom to do whatever she wants with her own body" commits the fallacy of begging the question. This fallacy occurs when an argument's premises assume the truth of the conclusion instead of supporting it. In this case, the statement assumes that a woman must have the freedom to do whatever she wants with her body, which is essentially restating the conclusion ("abortion must be legal") without providing actual reasoning or evidence. The argument doesn't justify why abortion should be legal beyond restating the premise in different words.

In other words, the speaker is assuming that the right to control one's body automatically implies the right to have an abortion, without addressing the complex ethical or legal considerations involved.
explanationHi:
यह कथन "बेशक, गर्भपात को कानूनी होना ही चाहिए। आख़िरकार, एक महिला को अपने शरीर के साथ जो चाहे करने की आज़ादी होनी चाहिए" प्रश्न पूछने की भ्रांति पैदा करता है। यह भ्रांति तब होती है जब किसी तर्क का आधार निष्कर्ष का समर्थन करने के बजाय उसकी सच्चाई मान लेता है। इस मामले में, कथन मानता है कि एक महिला को अपने शरीर के साथ जो कुछ भी करना है उसे करने की स्वतंत्रता होनी चाहिए, जो अनिवार्य रूप से वास्तविक तर्क या सबूत प्रदान किए बिना निष्कर्ष ("गर्भपात कानूनी होना चाहिए") को दोहरा रहा है। अलग-अलग शब्दों में आधार को दोहराने से परे यह तर्क इस बात को प्रमाणित नहीं करता है कि गर्भपात कानूनी क्यों होना चाहिए।

दूसरे शब्दों में, वक्ता यह मान रहा है कि जटिल नैतिक या कानूनी विचारों को संबोधित किए बिना, किसी के शरीर को नियंत्रित करने का अधिकार स्वचालित रूप से गर्भपात कराने का अधिकार दर्शाता है।

explanationEn:
1. Repression Defined:

o Repression is a psychological defense mechanism proposed by Sigmund Freud, where distressing thoughts, memories, or feelings are unconsciously pushed out of conscious awareness to protect the individual from psychological discomfort or anxiety.

2. Priya’s Situation:

o Priya knows she did something embarrassing, meaning she has an awareness that the event occurred.

o However, she cannot recall the details of the incident, which suggests that her mind has repressed the memory to avoid the emotional distress associated with it.

3.Why Not Other Options?

o Amnesia (Option 2): Amnesia refers to a significant loss of memory due to injury, illness, or psychological trauma. Priya’s case does not involve a generalized inability to recall events; it is specific to one memory.

o Implicit Memory (Option 3): Implicit memory involves unconscious memories that influence actions, such as skills or habits. Priya’s scenario is about a conscious attempt to recall a specific episodic memory, not an unconscious influence.

o Interference (Option 4): Interference occurs when one memory competes with or disrupts the recall of another. There’s no evidence that another memory is interfering with Priya’s ability to remember the embarrassing event.

4.Repression as a Protective Mechanism:

o By repressing the embarrassing memory, Priya’s subconscious mind shields her from reliving feelings of humiliation or discomfort.

o This is common in situations where memories are tied to strong negative emotions .

textEn: When we describe how a media system should function in conformity with ideal values, it is labelled as?
textHi: जब हम वर्णन करते हैं कि एक मीडिया प्रणाली को आदर्श मूल्यों के अनुरूप कैसे कार्य करना चाहिए, तो इसे इस प्रकार लेबल किया जाता है?
explanationEn:
Normative theory refers to the study and analysis of how a media system

should ideally function in society, based on certain values, norms, or

principles. It outlines the standards that a media system is expected to

meet in order to fulfill its societal role in the most ethical and effective

way. This type of theory is concerned with what should be, rather than

what is, focusing on ideal behaviors, structures, and practices that media

systems should adopt.

For example, normative theories may advocate for media systems to

promote democracy, diversity, social justice, or the free flow of

information, often based on ethical principles like fairness and objectivity.

These theories are used to critique and guide the development of media

systems in a way that aligns with society's values and goals.

Other types of theories, such as social theory, focus on understanding

the dynamics and effects of media in society, comparative theory

involves comparing media systems across different societies, and

analytical theory is about examining how media systems work in

practice, often with a focus on specific components like media effects or

content analysis. Normative theory, however, is the one that emphasizes

how media systems should operate in accordance with ideal values.

textEn: Knowing the importance of metacognition, Richa decided she would try to focus her young students' attention on their own thinking skills. Richa knew by having her students "think" about their thinking they would eventually increase their metacognitive skills. Which one of the strategy should Richa employ?
textHi: मेटाकॉग्निशन के महत्व को जानते हुए, ऋचा ने फैसला किया कि वह अपने युवा छात्रों का ध्यान उनकी सोच कौशल पर केंद्रित करने की कोशिश करेगी। ऋचा को पता था कि अपने छात्रों को उनकी सोच के बारे में "सोचने" से वे अंततः अपने मेटाकॉग्निटिव कौशल को बढ़ाएंगे। ऋचा को इनमें से कौन सी रणनीति अपनानी चाहिए?
explanationEn:
A KWL Chart is a teaching strategy designed to engage students in metacognitive thinking by encouraging them to reflect on their knowledge, learning process, and learning outcomes. The chart consists of three columns:

K (What I Know): Students list what they already know about a topic, activating prior knowledge and establishing a foundation for new learning.

W (What I Want to Know): Students write questions or topics they are curious about, setting goals and guiding their focus during the learning process.

L (What I Learned): After completing the learning activity, students reflect on what they have learned and compare it to their initial understanding.

Why is the KWL Chart effective for metacognition?

Promotes Self-Awareness: It helps students become aware of their existing knowledge and learning gaps, fostering self-awareness about their thinking process.

Encourages Goal Setting: By identifying what they want to know, students take ownership of their learning journey.

Supports Reflection: Reviewing what they learned helps students evaluate how their understanding has changed and identify new questions or insights.

Builds Critical Thinking: Students actively monitor and assess their learning process, enhancing higher-order thinking skills.

Other Options:

(1) Overlearning involves practicing a skill or material extensively beyond initial mastery. While useful for retention, it does not directly address metacognition.

(3) Rote learning emphasizes memorization without understanding, which does not foster metacognitive skills.

(4) An algorithm refers to a step-by-step procedure to solve problems, which does not encourage students to think critically about their learning process.

Thus, the KWL Chart is the most appropriate strategy for helping students "think about their thinking" and improve their metacognitive skills.
explanationHi:
KWL चार्ट एक शिक्षण रणनीति है जिसे छात्रों को उनके ज्ञान, सीखने की प्रक्रिया और सीखने के परिणामों पर प्रतिबिंबित करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करके मेटाकॉग्निटिव सोच में संलग्न करने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है। चार्ट में तीन कॉलम हैं:

के (मैं क्या जानता हूं): छात्र किसी विषय के बारे में जो कुछ पहले से जानते हैं उसे सूचीबद्ध करते हैं, पूर्व ज्ञान को सक्रिय करते हैं और नई शिक्षा के लिए नींव स्थापित करते हैं।

डब्ल्यू (मैं क्या जानना चाहता हूं): छात्र ऐसे प्रश्न या विषय लिखते हैं जिनके बारे में वे उत्सुक होते हैं, लक्ष्य निर्धारित करते हैं और सीखने की प्रक्रिया के दौरान अपना ध्यान केंद्रित करते हैं।

एल (मैंने क्या सीखा): सीखने की गतिविधि पूरी करने के बाद, छात्र इस बात पर विचार करते हैं कि उन्होंने क्या सीखा है और इसकी तुलना अपनी प्रारंभिक समझ से करते हैं।

KWL चार्ट मेटाकॉग्निशन के लिए प्रभावी क्यों है?

आत्म-जागरूकता को बढ़ावा देता है: यह छात्रों को उनके मौजूदा ज्ञान और सीखने के अंतराल के बारे में जागरूक होने में मदद करता है, उनकी सोचने की प्रक्रिया के बारे में आत्म-जागरूकता को बढ़ावा देता है।

लक्ष्य निर्धारण को प्रोत्साहित करता है: वे जो जानना चाहते हैं उसकी पहचान करके, छात्र अपनी सीखने की यात्रा का स्वामित्व लेते हैं।

चिंतन का समर्थन करता है: उन्होंने जो सीखा है उसकी समीक्षा करने से छात्रों को यह मूल्यांकन करने में मदद मिलती है कि उनकी समझ कैसे बदल गई है और नए प्रश्नों या अंतर्दृष्टि की पहचान करते हैं।

आलोचनात्मक सोच का निर्माण करता है: छात्र सक्रिय रूप से अपनी सीखने की प्रक्रिया की निगरानी और मूल्यांकन करते हैं, उच्चतर- को बढ़ाते हैं।

आदेश सोच कौशल.

अन्य विकल्प:

(1) ओवरलर्निंग में प्रारंभिक महारत से परे बड़े पैमाने पर किसी कौशल या सामग्री का अभ्यास करना शामिल है। प्रतिधारण के लिए उपयोगी होते हुए भी, यह सीधे तौर पर मेटाकॉग्निशन को संबोधित नहीं करता है।

(3) रटना सीखने में बिना समझे याद करने पर जोर दिया जाता है, जो मेटाकॉग्निटिव कौशल को बढ़ावा नहीं देता है।

(4) एल्गोरिदम समस्याओं को हल करने के लिए चरण-दर-चरण प्रक्रिया को संदर्भित करता है, जो छात्रों को उनकी सीखने की प्रक्रिया के बारे में गंभीर रूप से सोचने के लिए प्रोत्साहित नहीं करता है।

इस प्रकार, KWL चार्ट छात्रों को "उनकी सोच के बारे में सोचने" और उनके मेटाकॉग्निटिव कौशल में सुधार करने में मदद करने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त रणनीति है।

explanationEn:
Narratives are sequential accounts of events or actions, told from a

particular viewpoint, which can be in the form of stories, reports, or

descriptions. They are a key method of communication that allows

individuals or groups to present experiences, facts, or events in a

structured, coherent manner. Narratives are often used in literature,

history, journalism, and everyday communication to convey

information or share personal experiences.

The sequence in a narrative typically includes a beginning, middle,

and end, which helps to establish a clear flow of events. The

viewpoint or perspective from which the story is told shapes how

the audience interprets and understands the events. For example, a

first-person narrative might offer an intimate, personal perspective,

while a third-person narrative can provide a broader, more objective

view.

In summary, narratives are crucial for storytelling, reporting, and

communicating experiences in a structured way, and they are

characterized by their sequential nature and the specific viewpoint

from which they are presented.

textEn: According to Nyaya (Classical school of logic) which of the following step of inference corresponds to Upanaya?
textHi: न्याय (शास्त्रीय तर्कशास्त्र विद्यालय) के अनुसार अनुमान का निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा चरण उपनय से मेल खाता है?
optionsEn: Whatever has smoke has fire, e.g. an oven
The hill has smoke which is invariably associated with fire
optionsHi: जिस चीज़ में धुआं है उसमें आग है, जैसे एक ओवन
पहाड़ी पर धुआं है जो हमेशा आग से जुड़ा रहता है
explanationEn:
In the Nyaya school of logic, Upanaya refers to the step of inference where the major premise or general rule is applied to a specific instance. This is part of the process of deriving a conclusion from premises, where the premise establishes a universally known fact or law that can be applied to a particular case.

In the context of the example provided:

The statement "The hill has smoke which is invariably associated with fire" is the major premise, suggesting that smoke is a sign that fire is present. This is a universally recognized fact or law, which is why it represents Upanaya.

The major premise here is: "Whatever has smoke has fire." This premise, which generalizes the relationship between smoke and fire, is then applied to the specific instance of the hill having smoke, leading to the inference that the hill has fire.

Thus, Upanaya is the step where this general rule (about smoke and fire) is invoked to connect the observed phenomenon (smoke on the hill) with the conclusion (the hill has fire). The other options do not correctly represent this logical step, as they either present the observation itself or a restatement of the inference.

न्याय स्कूल ऑफ लॉजिक में, उपनय अनुमान के चरण को संदर्भित करता है जहां प्रमुख आधार या सामान्य नियम को एक विशिष्ट उदाहरण पर लागू किया जाता है। यह परिसर से निष्कर्ष निकालने की प्रक्रिया का हिस्सा है, जहां आधार एक सार्वभौमिक रूप से ज्ञात तथ्य या कानून स्थापित करता है जिसे किसी विशेष मामले पर लागू किया जा सकता है।

दिए गए उदाहरण के संदर्भ में:

यह कथन "पहाड़ी में धुआं है जो हमेशा आग से जुड़ा होता है" प्रमुख आधार है, जो बताता है कि धुआं एक संकेत है कि आग मौजूद है। यह एक सर्वमान्य तथ्य या नियम है, इसीलिए यह उपनय का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है।

यहां प्रमुख आधार यह है: "जिसमें धुआं है उसमें आग है।" यह आधार, जो धुएं और आग के बीच संबंध को सामान्यीकृत करता है, फिर पहाड़ी पर धुआं होने के विशिष्ट उदाहरण पर लागू किया जाता है, जिससे यह अनुमान लगाया जाता है कि पहाड़ी में आग है।

इस प्रकार, उपनय वह चरण है जहां देखी गई घटना (पहाड़ी पर धुआं) को निष्कर्ष (पहाड़ी पर आग है) के साथ जोड़ने के लिए इस सामान्य नियम (धुएं और आग के बारे में) का आह्वान किया जाता है। अन्य विकल्प इस तार्किक कदम का सही ढंग से प्रतिनिधित्व नहीं करते हैं, क्योंकि वे या तो स्वयं अवलोकन प्रस्तुत करते हैं या अनुमान का पुनर्कथन प्रस्तुत करते हैं।

textEn: Find the next number in the number series: 48, 24, 72, 36, 108, ?
explanationEn:
Let's analyze the given sequence: 48, 24, 72, 36, 108, ?

Notice the pattern alternates between dividing and

multiplying by certain factors:

48 ÷ 2 = 24 (Divide by 2)

24 × 3 = 72 (Multiply by 3)

72 ÷ 2 = 36 (Divide by 2)

36 × 3 = 108 (Multiply by 3)

Following this pattern, the next step should be to divide by 2:

108 ÷ 2 = 54

Thus, the next number in the series is 54.

108 ÷ 2 = 54

textEn: Which one of the following is a chemical parameter to measure the water quality?
textHi: जल की गुणवत्ता मापने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा एक रासायनिक पैरामीटर है?
explanationEn:
• Water quality is evaluated based on three primary parameters: physical, chemical, and biological. Among these, hardness is a chemical parameter that measures the concentration of certain minerals, primarily calcium and magnesium ions, in the water. Below is a detailed explanation:

1. Hardness as a Chemical Parameter:

o Hardness is caused by dissolved salts of calcium (Ca² ⁺ ) and magnesium (Mg² ⁺ ) in the water.

o It is a chemical characteristic that affects water's suitability for household and industrial uses.

o Hard water requires more soap for cleaning and can form scale deposits in pipes and appliances.

2. Other Options:

o Turbidity (Option 1): Turbidity is a physical parameter that measures the cloudiness or haziness of water caused by suspended solids.

o Temperature (Option 2): Temperature is also a physical parameter that affects the rate of chemical reactions and biological processes in water.

o Color (Option 4): Color is another physical parameter indicating the presence of organic material or dissolved metals but is not a chemical measurement.

3. Importance of Measuring Hardness:

o Excess hardness can damage household appliances and reduce the efficiency of industrial processes.

o It also impacts the taste and palatability of drinking water.

• Thus, hardness is a chemical parameter critical for assessing the quality of water, distinguishing it from other physical parameters like turbidity, temperature, and color.

ध्यान:

• पानी की गुणवत्ता का मूल्यांकन तीन प्राथमिक मापदंडों के आधार पर किया जाता है: भौतिक, रासायनिक और जैविक। इनमें कठोरता एक रासायनिक पैरामीटर है जो पानी में कुछ खनिजों, मुख्य रूप से कैल्शियम और मैग्नीशियम आयनों की सांद्रता को मापता है। नीचे एक विस्तृत विवरण दिया गया है:

1. रासायनिक पैरामीटर के रूप में कठोरता:

o कठोरता पानी में घुले कैल्शियम (Ca² ⁺ ) और मैग्नीशियम (Mg² ⁺ ) के लवण के कारण होती है।

o यह एक रासायनिक विशेषता है जो घरेलू और औद्योगिक उपयोग के लिए पानी की उपयुक्तता को प्रभावित करती है।

o कठोर जल को सफाई के लिए अधिक साबुन की आवश्यकता होती है और यह पाइपों और उपकरणों में स्केल जमा कर सकता है।

2. अन्य विकल्प:

o गंदलापन (विकल्प 1): गंदलापन एक भौतिक पैरामीटर है जो निलंबित ठोस पदार्थों के कारण पानी के बादल या धुंधलेपन को मापता है।

o तापमान (विकल्प 2): तापमान भी एक भौतिक पैरामीटर है जो पानी में रासायनिक प्रतिक्रियाओं और जैविक प्रक्रियाओं की दर को प्रभावित करता है।

o रंग (विकल्प 4): रंग एक अन्य भौतिक पैरामीटर है जो कार्बनिक पदार्थ या विघटित धातुओं की उपस्थिति का संकेत देता है लेकिन यह कोई रासायनिक माप नहीं है।

3. कठोरता मापने का महत्व:

o अत्यधिक कठोरता घरेलू उपकरणों को नुकसान पहुंचा सकती है और औद्योगिक प्रक्रियाओं की दक्षता को कम कर सकती है।

o यह पीने के पानी के स्वाद और स्वादिष्टता को भी प्रभावित करता है।

• इस प्रकार, कठोरता एक रासायनिक पैरामीटर है जो पानी की गुणवत्ता का आकलन करने, इसे अन्य भौतिक मापदंडों जैसे मैलापन, तापमान और रंग से अलग करने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है।

explanationEn:
To decode the pattern used in the given code, let's

analyze how the word GREAT is transformed into

ETCCR step by step:

Compare the corresponding letters: G → E: Shift 2 steps backward in the alphabetical

sequence. R → T: Shift 2 steps forward. E → C: Shift 2 steps backward. A → C: Shift 2 steps forward. T → R: Shift 2 steps backward.

Observe the pattern:

Alternate backward and forward shifts by 2

positions in the alphabet.

Applying the same pattern to the word FROWN: F → D (shift 2 steps backward)

R → T (shift 2 steps forward) O → M (shift 2 steps backward) W → Y (shift 2 steps forward) N → L (shift 2 steps backward) Thus, FROWN is coded as DTMYL.

textEn: The style that involves a student’s tendency to take over time to respond on the accuracy of answers is known as-
textHi: वह शैली जिसमें उत्तर की सटीकता पर प्रतिक्रिया देने के लिए छात्र की समय लेने की प्रवृत्ति शामिल होती है, कहलाती है
explanationEn:
Reflective style refers to the approach where a student takes extra time to consider and evaluate the accuracy of their answers before responding. Students with this style tend to reflect carefully on the information they have, often thinking critically about their responses to ensure they are correct. They prioritize accuracy and understanding over speed, which can lead to a more thoughtful and thorough approach to problem-solving and decision-making.

In contrast to impulsive style, where responses are given quickly without much thought, the reflective style requires a deliberate and measured consideration of the information. This style can be especially helpful in situations that demand careful analysis and in- depth understanding, such as academic tests, discussions, and complex problem-solving tasks.

While this style may sometimes lead to longer response times, it is often associated with deeper learning and greater retention of information, as the student has taken the time to process and internalize the material. Reflective learners may also be more self- aware of their learning process, allowing them to correct mistakes and refine their understanding over time.

textEn: The criterion of 'credibility' in qualitative research is equivalent to which of the following criteria in quantitative research?
textHi: गुणात्मक अनुसंधान में 'विश्वसनीयता' का मानदंड मात्रात्मक अनुसंधान में निम्नलिखित में से किस मानदंड के बराबर है?
explanationEn:
In qualitative research, credibility refers to the confidence in the truth of the findings. It is about how well the researcher has ensured that their interpretations and conclusions are accurate and reflect the reality of the participants' experiences.

In quantitative research, the criterion most equivalent to credibility is internal validity.

Internal validity refers to the extent to which the results of a study can be attributed to the manipulations of the independent variable, rather than to other potential confounding factors. In other words, it measures whether the study is truly measuring what it claims to measure, and whether the results are trustworthy and not influenced by other variables.

Thus, just as credibility ensures the accuracy and trustworthiness of qualitative research findings, internal validity ensures the accuracy and trustworthiness of quantitative research results.

Other options:

External validity refers to the generalizability of the research findings to broader populations or settings, which is different from credibility.

Objectivity in quantitative research involves the researcher remaining unbiased and neutral, which isn't directly equivalent to credibility in qualitative research.Reliability in quantitative research refers to the consistency of the measurement process, which is more concerned with the stability of results rather than their truthfulness or credibility.

Therefore, internal validity is the best match for credibility in qualitative research.

textEn: If the selling price of Rs. 623 results in a discount of 11% on the market price of an item, at what price should the item be sold to offer a discount of 19%?
textHi: यदि विक्रय मूल्य रु. 623 के परिणामस्वरूप किसी वस्तु के बाजार मूल्य पर 11% की छूट मिलती है, 19% की छूट देने के लिए वस्तु को किस कीमत पर बेचा जाना चाहिए?
explanationEn:
Step 1: Find the Market Price (MP)

We know:

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 623

Discount = 11%

Formula:

SP = MP × (1 - Discount / 100)

Substitute the values:

623 = MP × (1 - 11 / 100)

623 = MP × 0.89

MP = 623 / 0.89

MP = 700

Market Price (MP) = Rs. 700

Step 2: Calculate SP for a 19% Discount

We know:

MP = Rs. 700

Discount = 19%

Formula:

SP = MP × (1 - Discount / 100)

Substitute the values: SP = 700 × (1 - 19 / 100)

SP = 700 × 0.81

SP = 567

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 567

Step 1: Find the total rice consumption per day for 40

people

Thus, the rice consumed per day by 40 people is:

Rice per day for 40 people = 320 kg / 50 days = 6.4

kg/day

Step 2: Calculate the rice consumption per person per day

Rice consumption per person per day:

Rice per person per day = 6.4 kg / 40 people = 0.16 kg/day

per person

Step 3: Find the number of days required for 30 people to

consume 80 kg of rice

Now, 30 people will consume 80 kg of rice. The total rice

consumption per day for 30 people is:

Rice per day for 30 people = 30 * 0.16 = 4.8 kg/day

Now, the number of days required to consume 80 kg of rice

Days = 80 kg / 4.8 kg/day = 16.67 days

16.67 days = 16 𝟐 / 𝟑 days

textEn:
Biomass

A. is a carbon cycle neutral fuel

B. has significantly higher calorific value then coal

C. can be converted in solid, liquid and gaseous fuels

D. can be converted into Producer Gas

E. cannot be obtained from energy crops

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
textHi:
बायोमास

A. एक कार्बन चक्र तटस्थ ईंधन है

बी. का ऊष्मीय मान कोयले की तुलना में काफी अधिक है

C. को ठोस, तरल और गैसीय ईंधन में परिवर्तित किया जा सकता है

D. को उत्पादक गैस में परिवर्तित किया जा सकता है

ई. ऊर्जा फसलों से प्राप्त नहीं किया जा सकता

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनें:
explanationEn:
A. Biomass is a carbon cycle neutral fuel:

This is true. Biomass is considered a carbon-neutral fuel because the carbon dioxide (CO ₂ ) released during combustion is offset by the CO ₂ absorbed during the plant’s growth. This is a key environmental benefit of biomass as a renewable energy source.

B. Biomass has significantly higher calorific value than coal:

This is false. Biomass typically has a lower calorific value than coal. While biomass can provide significant energy, coal generally has a higher energy density per unit weight.

C. Biomass can be converted into solid, liquid, and gaseous fuels:

This is true. Biomass can be converted into different types of fuels. It can remain as solid fuel (e.g., wood pellets), be converted into liquid fuels (e.g., bioethanol, biodiesel), and also converted into gaseous fuels (e.g., biogas, producer gas).

D. Biomass can be converted into Producer Gas:

This is true. Biomass can be processed through a process called gasification to produce producer gas, which is a mixture of carbon monoxide (CO), hydrogen (H ₂ ), and methane (CH ₄ ) and can be used as a fuel for energy production.

E. Biomass cannot be obtained from energy crops:

This is false. Biomass can indeed be obtained from energy crops specifically grown for bioenergy production, such as switchgrass, miscanthus, and fast-growing trees like poplar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2: A, C and D Only.
explanationHi:
A. बायोमास एक कार्बन चक्र तटस्थ ईंधन है:

यह सच है। बायोमास को कार्बन-तटस्थ ईंधन माना जाता है क्योंकि दहन के दौरान निकलने वाले कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड (CO ₂ ) की भरपाई पौधे के विकास के दौरान अवशोषित CO ₂ से हो जाती है। नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा स्रोत के रूप में बायोमास का यह एक प्रमुख पर्यावरणीय लाभ है।

बी. बायोमास का कैलोरी मान कोयले की तुलना में काफी अधिक है:

यह गलत है। बायोमास का कैलोरी मान आमतौर पर कोयले की तुलना में कम होता है। जबकि बायोमास महत्वपूर्ण ऊर्जा प्रदान कर सकता है, कोयले में आमतौर पर प्रति यूनिट वजन में उच्च ऊर्जा घनत्व होता है।

C. बायोमास को ठोस, तरल और गैसीय ईंधन में परिवर्तित किया जा सकता है:

यह सच है। बायोमास को विभिन्न प्रकार के ईंधन में परिवर्तित किया जा सकता है। यह ठोस ईंधन (जैसे, लकड़ी के गोले) के रूप में रह सकता है, तरल ईंधन (जैसे, बायोएथेनॉल, बायोडीजल) में परिवर्तित हो सकता है, और गैसीय ईंधन (जैसे, बायोगैस, उत्पादक गैस) में भी परिवर्तित हो सकता है।

D. बायोमास को उत्पादक गैस में परिवर्तित किया जा सकता है:

यह सच है। उत्पादक गैस का उत्पादन करने के लिए बायोमास को गैसीकरण नामक प्रक्रिया के माध्यम से संसाधित किया जा सकता है, जो कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड (CO), हाइड्रोजन (H ₂ ), और मीथेन (CH ₄ ) का मिश्रण है और ऊर्जा उत्पादन के लिए ईंधन के रूप में उपयोग किया जा सकता है।

ई. ऊर्जा फसलों से बायोमास प्राप्त नहीं किया जा सकता:

यह गलत है। बायोमास वास्तव में बायोएनर्जी उत्पादन के लिए विशेष रूप से उगाई जाने वाली ऊर्जा फसलों से प्राप्त किया जा सकता है, जैसे कि स्विचग्रास, मिसकैंथस, और तेजी से बढ़ने वाले पेड़ जैसे चिनार।

इसलिए, सही उत्तर विकल्प 2: केवल ए, सी और डी है।

explanationEn:

Hidden symbol: This term is not commonly used in non- verbal communication theory.

Effective symbol: This term generally refers to symbols that effectively communicate a message, but it is not a standard term for abstract representations.

Ideational symbol: While this may be a close concept, abstract symbol is the more precise term in this context.

Thus, abstract symbols are those that represent ideas or thoughts in a non-verbal form, making Option 3 the correct answer.

Floods are normal events that cause damage. As rivers carve and shape the landscape, they build broad floodplains, level expanses that are periodically inundated.
